content.text: {"grade": 2, "complete": false, "main_gap": "The central Lemma (that σ(x)=P(x)∩Q is good for every term x) — the entire difficulty of the problem — is asserted with \"details omitted\" and never proved.", "errors": [{"description": "The key lemma, which is the crux of the problem (showing primes larger than a_1 are irrelevant to the compatibility condition), is stated without proof; 'standard' is unjustified and the referenced repair construction R p^k never appears in the argument.", "quote": "**Proof.** Induction over the sequence terms in increasing order (standard; details omitted). \\(\\square\\)"}, {"description": "The write-up admits the lemma is only supported by numerical experiments, which earn no credit; the claim that the argument 'proves it independently' is false since no argument is given.", "quote": "These computations only test the lemma; the argument above proves it independently."}, {"description": "Minor: the final step asserts every length-L interval in [A,∞) contains exactly T terms via 'each residue modulo L once'; this needs (4) applied to the residue-class characterization, stated but not spelled out (repairable).", "quote": "Every interval of \\(L\\) consecutive integers contained in \\([A,\\infty)\\) contains each residue modulo \\(L\\) once and therefore contains exactly \\(T\\) sequence terms, by (4)."}], "notes": "The surrounding framework (characterization (1), upward-closed goodness, periodicity mod ∏_{p≤A} p, and the counting argument) is correct and cleanly done, but it is only a reduction; the essential lemma is missing entirely."}
